learning_outcomes.text: Ability for the design and management of applied experimentation procedures, especially for the determination of thermodynamic and transport properties and modeling of phenomena and systems in the field of chemical engineering, systems with fluid flow, heat transfer, mass transfer operations, chemical reaction kinetics and reactors.
Correctly use terms specific to Instrumental Analysis.
Recognize and correctly handle the material and equipment commonly used in Instrumental Analysis.
Write a report with the results obtained in the resolution of each analytical problem.
Work with discipline and make decisions autonomously.
Use one's own language with appropriate rigor to communicate orally or in writing.
Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the basic aspects of working with Instrumental Techniques.
Recognize and correctly handle the material and equipment commonly used in Instrumental Analysis.
Develop a detailed work plan and carry it out respecting safety regulations in a chemical laboratory.
Write a report with the results obtained for each analytical problem posed.

syllabus_topics: Enzymatic determination of glucose in food
Determination of metals by atomic absorption spectroscopy
Analysis of sodium and potassium by flame emission spectroscopy
Determination of elemental traces by ICP-MS
Ion selective electrodes: application to fluoride determination
Separation and determination of compounds by gas chromatography and/or liquid chromatography

assessment_methods.method: Activities performed in the laboratory (Professional attitudes, execution of general procedures, safety and environmental management of reagents and products)
Contents of Classroom Practices (Laboratory reports, exercises, questions, activities)

assessment_rules: To pass the course, a minimum grade of 4 out of 10 must be obtained in each assessable aspect. The final grade must be equal to or greater than 5 out of 10. For extraordinary examinations, a final exam will be conducted, consisting of a written test and, if applicable, a practical exam. The extraordinary exam will be weighted 40% for questions related to all practical contents and 60% for an oral presentation.
